mainClaim: Independent contractor status in gig work denies workers essential protections while giving companies control without responsibilities
evidence: No verified source is cited for this argument. The argument rests on reasoning: independent contractor status leaves workers carrying vehicle costs and income risk without benefits, while platform algorithms set pay and dispatch work.
supportingPoints: Workers bear all risk: vehicle costs, insurance, maintenance, no unemployment protection
No discrimination protections - apps can deactivate workers without recourse
Asymmetric information - platforms control all data about earnings and opportunities
Creates two-tier labor system with second-class workers
limitations: The earlier UC Berkeley study, leaked-data and AB5 figures could not be traced to published sources and were removed. Other figures in the supporting points have not been checked. Some workers genuinely prefer flexibility and multiple platforms. Optimal classification may be neither pure employee nor contractor. Need portable benefits solutions. Implementation challenges in California show regulatory complexity.
